headline: The DOJ and Commerce Department are investigating Megaspeed, the firm at the center of Nvidia's spy scandal, as Jensen Huang agreed to testify before Congress and UNIDIR warned of open-source AI's risks to international security.

points.text: The Justice and Commerce Departments said they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation.
Jensen Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will testify before Congress in early December, as lawmakers seek answers on whether Nvidia's AI chips reached China improperly.
ChinaTalk asked whether the Bureau of Industry and Security's crackdown means the era of 'compute leakage' to China is over.
UNIDIR warned that open-source AI remains an under-addressed international security issue, with proliferation risks among malicious non-state actors growing rapidly.
UNIDIR helped Cabo Verde conduct a national weapons and ammunition management baseline assessment, in partnership with the Economic Community of West African States.
OpenAI gave NATO access to its most advanced cybersecurity AI, which operators used this month to build and deploy AI agents in an exercise.
Wired reported on two ex-Google and Apple executives who say AI guided them in building a billion-dollar lethal munitions manufacturing business.
